articles.title: CAFC Says District Court Failed to Provide Sufficient Reasoning for Denying Sanctions, Attorney’s Fees
articles.description: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (CAFC) issued a precedential decision Wednesday vacating and remanding a district court ruling that had denied Pen-Tech Associates, Inc.’s motion for sanctions and attorney’s fees due to Epic Tech, LLC’s allegedly frivolous infringement claims. The CAFC found the district court had provided “insufficient detail to permit meaningful review.” The post CAFC Says District Court Failed to Provide Sufficient Reasoning for Denying Sanctions, Attorney’s Fees appeared first on IPWatchdog.com | Patents & Intellectual Property Law.
